condition: progressive difficulty swallowing solid meat over 6 weeks needing endoscopy referral
level_rationale: Solid meat getting stuck behind the breastbone at every dinner for 6 weeks in a 63-year-old adult who still swallows water and soup easily indicates progressive mechanical esophageal solid-food dysphagia warranting prompt primary-care physician evaluation and urgent upper gastrointestinal endoscopy referral rather than home self-care or immediate emergency resuscitation, whereas a single hurried bite of steamed rice pausing behind the breastbone for 3 seconds once last month with easy swallowing otherwise represents a benign transient bolus pause requiring only routine self-care.

design_note: Three atomic positive reference facts cover age 63, easy swallowing of water and soup, and solid meat getting stuck behind the breastbone at every dinner for 6 weeks without naming esophageal stricture or cancer, with a 1-word span difference (14 vs 15 words). Under reviewer_notes Rule A first choice and Rule D (avoiding spitting-saliva overlap with r11-098), reducing f3 to a single 3-second retrosternal pause after a hurried bite of steamed rice once last month stays inside the swallowing case with zero stated negatives and shifts care cleanly from doctor evaluation (level 2) to routine self-care (level 1).
